reel.hook: TAIWAN VS [SHORT SELLERS] AFTER A 17.5% DROP
reel.topic: Asian governments stepping into their stock markets after last week's AI-led selloff. Taiwan: the Taiex lost 17.5% (7,641.83 points) in the week to Friday 20 Nov and closed at 36,033.29 (CNA via Seoul Economic Daily; Bytes Europe), its worst week in 35 years (Bloomberg via The Star; 'since 1991', Bloomberg via TNW). On Saturday 21 Nov the Financial Supervisory Commission banned short sales below the previous day's closing price for all listed stocks from Monday 23 Nov, covering margin short sales and borrowed shares, with hedging by securities and futures firms exempt; it raised the short-sale margin to 150% from 130% and stopped taking applications for new put warrants (Bloomberg via The Star and TNW; stockanalysis.com citing the FSC release). It is the third round of curbs this month (9 Nov, 19 Nov); 'Two earlier rounds of short-selling restrictions this month have so far failed to stabilise the market' (Bloomberg via The Star). The NT$500 billion (about US$15 billion) National Financial Stabilization Fund has been buying since 6 Nov (Bloomberg via TNW; RTI). Monday 23 Nov: the Taiex 'opened lower but closed up 778 points, or 2.16%, at 36,811.89'; Premier Cho Jung-tai said the government is willing to review enlarging the fund, after some commentators and lawmakers urged NT$1 trillion, and that existing resources remain sufficient and fundamentals are solid; Economy Minister Kung Ming-hsin attributed the sell-off to global factors: doubts over sustained AI spending, possible tighter limits on computing power for China, personnel changes at Nvidia and a possible Fed rate rise (all RTI, 23 Nov 18:42). South Korea: Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il chaired an emergency meeting on Sunday 22 Nov and said the stock market stabilisation fund (10.76 trillion won, Korea JoongAng Daily; 'about 10 trillion won', Seoul Economic Daily) would be made ready; daily buyback limits are eased for three months from Tuesday 24 Nov; no new short-selling limits, stronger enforcement instead (Korea JoongAng Daily, CoinCentral, Reuters via The Edge Malaysia). The Kospi closed Monday down 161.42 points (3.31%) at 4,708.54 (Yonhap caption in Korea JoongAng Daily; Lapaas Voice). China: the Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing exchanges cut the minimum margin ratio for margin financing to 80% from 100% from 30 Nov (Reuters and Bloomberg via stockanalysis.com; Lapaas Voice; Stephen Innes citing Reuters). The sceptical view: Stephen Innes writes that such steps can make it harder to sell and easier to buy but 'Neither necessarily makes them want to own the market'. Next: US PCE inflation on Wednesday 25 Nov (Kiplinger, TipRanks); the Fed meets 8-9 Dec (TipRanks) with a rate rise priced at over 90% last week (CME FedWatch via Kiplinger: above 97%; AND Magazine: more than 90%).
